reasons.C: Long, clause-laden sentences joined by semicolons and 'since/because', first-person hedges ('It seems to me', 'I suspect', 'perhaps'), 'we might ask' cadence and no dashes all match the passage's measured, tentative movement.
reasons.D: Close in sentence length, hedging and a question opening, but the dash-bracketed list and the detached one-line aphoristic closing paragraph are foreign to the passage and lean towards a flourish it never makes.
reasons.A: Right register and long periodic sentences, but repeated dashes, less first-person hedging and a more expository, assured stance put it a step further from the author's tentative voice.
reasons.B: Short declarative sentences, rhetorical question lists, imperatives ('So ask', 'Then check') and small paragraphs give a brisk how-to voice quite unlike the passage's long, hedged reflection.
